entry.title: Improve Build Apps UIs to Allow Keyboard Click / Control Focus
entry.content:
I was doing this great tutorial by my colleagues @Rekha_DR and @shrinivasan_neelamegam about creating a chatbot using Build Apps and AI Core, a topic they delivered in the SAP TechEd developer keynote in 2024: https://github.com/SAP-samples/teched2024-developer-keynote/blob/main/topics/DEV100A-build-chatbot-apps-aicore/README.md

It worked perfectly. 

The tutorial let you create a chatbot where you typed a prompt, got an answer, and then could send a new prompt, like a regular chatbot. (By the way, one of the clever designs of theirs was that the context of the conversation was always sent back to the AI Core with every subsequent prompt.)

I thought what would make the app even more helpful would be:

  • To be able to press Enter after typing in each prompt.
  • To place the cursor automatically in the prompt input box so the user could just start typing the next prompt.

 

Allow Enter Instead of Button Click

To do this, you first want to create a custom event for the logic that you want connected to the button click / Enter press.

Drag a Receive Event flow function onto the canvas.

Set the Event Source to Fired from "Trigger Event", and give the event a name, like SendChat.

Attach your logic (in this case the calls to AI Core) to the event.

Now all that's left is to trigger this event when the user clicks the button, or presses Enter. 

For the button click, select the button click, drag a Trigger Event flow function, and connect it to your Component Tap event for the button.

Configure the Trigger Event flow function by selecting your new event to be triggered.

To enable the logic to be triggered by pressing Enter, highlight your input box, and create the following logic on the input box's onKeyPress event.

To the onKeyPress event, add an If Condition flow function with the following formula:

outputs["Receive event"].eventValue == "Enter"

And then to the top output add a Trigger Event, configured the same as for the button click logic above.

 

Place Cursor in Input Box

Every time I send a prompt, I want the cursor to return to the input box so I can type in the next prompt.

Install the Focus Input flow function from the Marketplace.

After the logic for sending the prompt and receiving the answer from AI Core, add this flow function and specify the input box.

😽

entry.title: Use SAP Integration Suite to connect SAP and AWS services
entry.content:
Bridging the gap between SAP and 3rd party systems 

Everyone already knows that SAP Integration Suite is the election tool to connect your SAP services. But did you know that it is also your tool to integrate Everything, Everywhere, All in One Place? (yes, almost like the Oscar award winning movie 🏆)

Use SAP Integration Suite to connect SAP and AWS services is a new official SAP Discovery Center Mission that focus on showcasing how easy it is to integrate not only SAP systems but also non-SAP systems using SAP Integration Suite. 

For this mission, we decided to use the AWS platform as the example of third-party cloud services provider, but the same rational with this set of best practices and capabilities can be used to integrate with other cloud providers. By following the cards provided in the mission, you will see step-by-step how you can start to integrate an application developed with SAP BTP development tools with AWS services, such as S3 for image storage and Rekognition for image identification.
You can even use a SAP BTP Trial account to perform the SAP BTP parts of the mission, even though you will always still require also an AWS account to connect with the S3 and Rekognition services (and IAM for user and roles management on the AWS side). Either if you are a technical user or more of a business user interested in rapid application development, cloud integration strategies and/or AI-powered business solution, this mission is for you!

The following architecture shows the big picture of what the final result of the mission should look like, seamlessly combining the best of both SAP BTP and AWS platforms:

 

 

Use Case Description

The use case followed trough out the mission focuses in enabling a Supplier to donate surplus food ingredients through an AI-powered mobile and web application built using SAP Build Apps, a low-code/no-code solution within SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), seamlessly integrated with AWS capabilities for storage and artificial intelligence–based image recognition. For the integration part, you will leverage and combine different integration capabilities that are part of the SAP Integration Suite. The intended outcome of the use case is to minimize food waste while simplifying the donation process and facilitating redistribution to organizations in need.

Solution Components:

  • SAP Build Apps: The low-code/no-code application development service used to create the application (frontend and logic) where the Supplier can donate the surplus ingredients by taking or uploading photos 
  • SAP Integration Suite: The secure and centralized integration management service for all your integrations, making them easier to manage, monitor and troubleshoot
  • Amazon S3: The Amazon service for simplified and cost-effective image storage capabilities
  • Amazon Rekognition: The Amazon service for AI-powered identification and categorization, in this case used to identify the ingredients in the images taken or uploaded from the application to a S3 bucket

The Use Case Flow:

  1. A Supplier captures or uploads an image of surplus ingredients through the mobile/web app (developed with SAP Build Apps)
  2. The image is securely stored in Amazon S3 via SAP Integration Suite (using Cloud integration with the Amazon Web Services Adapter and API Management capabilities)
  3. Also via SAP Integration Suite, the app then calls Amazon Rekognition to automatically identify and categorize the ingredient present in the image (using Cloud Integration and API Management capabilities)
  4. The results are sent back to the app and ready for further processing

 

 

Learning Outcomes

By completing this Discovery Center Mission, you'll gain practical experience in:

  • Building low-code applications with SAP Build Apps
  • Configuring SAP Integration Suite for AWS connectivity
  • Implementing secure cloud-to-cloud integrations
  • Leveraging AI services for business process automation
  • Managing integration flows and monitoring capabilities

Getting Started

Once you open and start the Mission, you will see in the Project Board the different cards that will guide you step-by-step, divided in 7 columns.

Make sure you fullfill all the requirements indicated in the SET UP and PREPARE columns. After that, you can start with the EXECUTE columns. You will first explore the Security Materials area and the Cloud Integration and API Management capabilities of SAP Integration Suite (in the Execute - Security Material and Integration Flows), and then you will get to visually create a simple app with SAP Build Apps (in Execute - Build app) that will call the iFlows created before in SAP Integration Suite.
After finishing the mission, don't forget to mark all the cards as completed and we encourage you to leave your feedback and share your experiences with the rest of the SAP Community. 

And now, for those who saw the movie Everything Everywhere All at Once, DON'T "Just be a rock" and start the mission here!  ->  SAP Discovery Center Missions - Use SAP Integration Suite to connect SAP and AWS services

entry.title: SAPUI5 – Pagination in Table on button click using S/4 Hana cloud oData service
entry.content:
Hi, in this blog I’m going to explain the pagination in Table with S/4 Hana cloud oData service with flexibility to control number of visible rows per page. 

 

In this example, I am using S/4 Hana cloud oData service through destination. I have 621 records in Product entity set and by default, I have to display 10 records per click and user can change number of visible rows. So, I have placed four nav buttons for First page, Previous page, Next page and Last page with page count information and drop down for number of visible rows and then some magical code.

 

Firstly, create new front end web and mobile application with zproducts name.

 

In the canvas, give title as Products and remove bottom text.

 

Add Integration:

Go to Integrations tab and select add integration and then select BTP destinations under sap systems.

In BTP destinations, select our S/4 Hana cloud service destination i.e., S4HANA_Joule_Product and select A_Product entityset. Now Select install integration and enable data entity. You can browse real data by selecting browse real data. Click on save at top right corner.

 

Add Variables:

Now go to Variables tab and go to page variables and select add page variable and choose from scratch.

Add variable noOfVisibleRows with value type Number with initial value 10.

Similarly add variables totalNoOfRows with value type Number,

Variable currentPage with value type Number with initial value 1,

totalPages with value type Number with initial value 1 and

variable isRefresh with value type true/false with initial value false and Click on save at top right corner.

User Interface:

In User Interface, we install table with data adaptor from marketplace and assign our entity set to it to fetch the data and we will add new property to make table to load the data at each time when user clicks on nav buttons or change number of visible rows.

Go to User Interface tab and select marketplace and search for basic table with data adapter and install it. Drag and drop the basic table with data adapter to canvas and select configure and select A_product and add the required columns and in properties tab, at pagination in Object with properties, assign noOfVisibleRows page variable to page size, assign currentPage page variable to Page Number and click on save. Click on save and exit and save at top right corner.

Go to open in component template editor at bottom in properties tab and select properties and in properties, add new property Refresh of type true/false. Go to view and select add logic to Basic table with data adapter at bottom right corner. Drag and drop Receive event and select Internal property 'Refresh' changed and connect end of the receive event to start of get record collection. Click on save and exit. You can see Refresh property in properties tab.

 

 

Assign Refresh property with isRefresh page variable

 

Now select at page level and open logic canvas. Drag and drop record collection and connect to Page Mounted and assign A_Product to resource and for pagination make Include total count as true by selecting binding type as static values true/false.

 

Now drag and drop set page variable and select variable name as totalNoOfRows and assign formula outputs["Get record collection"].totalCount for value and connect end of get Record Collection top node to start of Set Page Variable node.

Similarly, drag and drop another set page variable for totalPages and assign formula CEIL(outputs["Get record collection"].totalCount / pageVars.noOfVisibleRows).

Add Nav Buttons:

Now drag and drop container at bottom of table and select layout as horizontal.

Drag and drop button inside the container and name it as First. For disabled, add formula IF(pageVars.currentPage > 1, false, true) and in logic convas, add two set page variables. One for currentPage and set the value to 1 and another for isRefresh and assign formula NOT(pageVars.isRefresh).

Similarly add another button inside the container and name it as Previous. For disabled, add formula IF(pageVars.currentPage > 1, false, true) and in logic convas, add two set page variables. One for currentPage and assign formula pageVars.currentPage – 1 and another for isRefresh and assign formula NOT(pageVars.isRefresh).

Add another button inside the container and name it as Next. For disabled, add formula IF(pageVars.currentPage < pageVars.totalPages, false, true) and in logic convas, add two set page variables. One for currentPage and assign formula pageVars.currentPage + 1 and another for isRefresh and assign formula NOT(pageVars.isRefresh).

Add another button inside the container and name it as Last. For disabled, add formula IF(pageVars.currentPage < pageVars.totalPages, false, true) and in logic convas, add two set page variables. One for currentPage and assign formula pageVars. totalPages and another for isRefresh and assign formula NOT(pageVars.isRefresh).

Drag and drop text after Previous button and for content add formula pageVars.currentPage + " / " + pageVars.totalPages.

Drag and drop Dropdown and give label text as No of Rows and select option list -> List of values and add value and give values 10, 25, 50, 100 and save. Make Placeholder text as empty.

In Logic pane of dropdown field, drag and drop set page variable and assign variable name to noOfVisibleRows and add formula IF(self.value, NUMBER(self.value), pageVars.noOfVisibleRows ) for value.

Similarly, drag and drop another page variable and assign currentpageno to it and value as 1.

Another page variable with totalpages and formula for value is CEIL(pageVars.totalNoOfRows / pageVars.noOfVisibleRows) and save at the top right corner.

Add another page variable with isRefresh with formula for value NOT(pageVars.isRefresh).

Preview Application:

Save at top right corner and click on preview and select open web preview. Now, you can see our application with pagination and flexibility to control number of visible rows per page.

 

 

By doing this, we can easily add pagination in Table on button click by consuming S/4 Hana cloud oData service with flexibility to control number of visible rows per page. 

 

That’s it!!!

entry.title: Enhancing Customer Data Accuracy with SAP DQM Address Validation in CX Sales and Service Cloud V2
entry.content:
Why Address Quality Matters in Customer Experience

In today’s customer-centric world, accurate address data is far more than a backend requirement — it directly impacts customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and compliance. Invalid or inconsistent addresses lead to failed deliveries, delayed services, poor agent productivity, and frustrated customers.

With SAP CX Service Cloud V2, organizations can significantly improve data quality by integrating SAP Data Quality Management (DQM) – Address Validation Service, ensuring that customer addresses are accurate, standardized, and validated in real time.

What is SAP DQM – Address Validation?

SAP DQM Address Validation is a cloud-based service that helps organizations:

  • Validate postal addresses in real time
  • Standardize address formats based on country-specific rules
  • Enrich address data with missing components
  • Reduce duplicates and incorrect records

The service supports global address validation across multiple countries, making it ideal for enterprises operating at scale.

Why Integrate DQM with CX Service Cloud V2?

CX Service Cloud V2 acts as the single source of truth for customer interactions. Ensuring clean address data at this layer brings several benefits:

Key Business Benefits

  • 🚀Faster case handling with fewer address-related corrections
  • 📦Reduced delivery failures and service disruptions
  • 😊Improved customer trust and experience
  • 📊Better reporting, analytics, and segmentation

Key Technical Benefits

  • Real-time validation during data entry
  • API-based integration aligned with SAP BTP standards
  • Reusable validation logic across multiple CX touchpoints

Prerequisites

Before enabling the DQM service, ensure the following are in place:

  • SAP BTP account (Cloud Foundry environment)
  • Entitlement to SAP Data Quality Management, microservices for location data
  • CX Service Cloud V2 tenant
  • Basic understanding of SAP BTP Destinations and API consumption
  • SAP Build Apps

Enable DQM Service in SAP BTP

  • Navigate to SAP BTP Cockpit
  • Go to Entitlements → Entity Assignments
  • Add entitlement for SAP Data Quality Management
  • Create a Service Instance for Address Validation

Configure Authentication & Access

DQM services are secured using OAuth 2.0:

  • Create a Service Key for the DQM instance
  • Capture:
    • Client ID
    • Client Secret
    • Token URL
    • API endpoint

These credentials are used by CX extensions or middleware to securely call the DQM API.

Create Destination in SAP BTP

Create an HTTP destination to consume the DQM service:

  • Authentication Type: OAuth2ClientCredentials
  • Token Service URL: From service key
  • Client ID / Secret: From service key
  • Target URL: DQM Address Validation endpoint

This destination enables secure and reusable connectivity from:

  • SAP Build Apps
  • SAP Build Process Automation
  • Custom CX extensions

Similarly create for SAP Service Cloud V2

Create SAP Build Apps Project

  • Open SAP Build Apps
  • Create a new project (Web or Responsive App)
  • Choose Blank App or Master-Detail template
  • Name it: CX_Address_Validation_App
  • Design your site as per you requirement 

Create Mashup in CX Service Cloud V2

  • Log in to CX Service Cloud V2
  • Navigate to:
    Administrator → Mashup Authoring
  • Click New Mashup
  • Provide:
    • Name: Address Validation – DQM
    • Type: URL Mashup
    • URL: Build Apps deployed URL

✔ Save the mashup.

Embedded Mashup in Account - CX Service Cloud V2

For a detailed walkthrough of the functionality, please refer to the video.
It showcases the embedded address validation experience in CX Service Cloud V2.

entry.title: Build custom Joule Agent to analyze blocked freight order in S/4HANA TM
entry.content:
In this blog, the objective is to build a custom Joule agent with multiple skills that analyzes a blocked freight order in the S/4HANA Transportation Management (TM) solution.

To keep the scenario simple, the agent analyzes blocks caused by time conflicts and explains them in simple business language.

What you will learn

By the end of this blog, you will understand:

  • The prerequisites for building this use case
  • How to expose TM documents as OData services consumable by Joule
  • How to create Build Actions, Joule Skills, and a Joule Agent
  • How to write basic instructions for the Joule Agent
  • How to test and fine-tune the agent

All of this can be done with minimal or no coding. With the right access and setup, even a business user can follow these steps and build a basic scenario in about 30 minutes. The approach is similar across S/4HANA solutions, with different OData services used to fetch backend data.

Let’s look at the high-level steps

  1. Pre-requisites
  2. Identify available CDS views in S/4HANA TM and wrap it with an OData service
  3. Configure SAP Cloud Connector – Joule (from public internet) needs secure communication channel to connect your ERP environment
  4. Define Destinations on your BTP subaccount - connect to the OData service via cloud connector
  5. Define Actions in Joule Studio
  6. Define Joule Skills
  7. Define Joule Agent
  8. Test!

Let’s look at the steps in detail.

  1. STEP 1: Pre-requisites

            You need the following to run this scenario,

  • An S/4HANA private or on-premise environment
  • Eclipse IDE with ABAP Development Toolkit (ADT) – see the tutorial if you haven’t done
  • SAP Cloud Connector installed in your landscape – follow this if haven’t done
  • An SAP BTP subaccount with Joule Studio (Joule studio is one of the components of SAP Build) – follow SAP Discovery Center Mission for steps to do that.

STEP 2: Identify available CDS views in S/4HANA TM and wrap it with an OData service

            Look at the SAP documentation for all available standard S/4HANA CDS views. For S/4HANA TM, see here. In this use case, we require data from Freight Order, its item and stop nodes. So, let’s login to S/4HANA system and create an OData service for the three CDS views.

Select a package and create a service definition

 

Select referenced object as the respective CDS view and create and activate the service definition for the three CDS views.

 

Once created the definition, create a service binding by right click on each definition. Follow the wizard and after creation, activate the binding and then publish it. You can see the service URL and note that down. You can as well test the service now.

 

STEP 3: Configure Cloud Connector

Login to your SAP Cloud connector and Configure cloud to On-premise for the subaccount you are going to use for Joule. ‘/’ expose all which is not ideal, but fine for testing environments.

 

STEP 4: Define Destinations on your BTP subaccount

Now login to your BTP sub-account and navigate to ConnectivityDestinations and create a destination of type ‘HTTP,’ proxytype ‘OnPremise’.

The URL must be constructed by combining virtual host URL in cloud connector with service end point. Also add additional properties as shown in the screenshot.

 

STEP 5: Define Build Actions

Now navigate to your Joule Studio (SAP Build) environment.

Navigate to the ConnectorsActions and create an action to fetch freight orders which are blocked.

Once you click create, select OData Destinations as API source. It will display all OData destinations defined in the subaccount. Pick the destination created in step 4.

 

It displays the available services in the underlying CDS view. Select Next and provide a meaningful name and description. Then navigate to the created action project.

 

Initially, the OData service will be with its basic definition. We need to add filter to fetch only filter blocked freight order (just pick execution blocked).

For this, click $filter parameter and then click Value F4 help in the popup. You can use condition editor or Text Expression.

 

Reduce output fields

In the Output tab:

  1. Select the Body parameter.
  2. Remove unnecessary fields.

For this scenario, keep only:

  • Order number
  • Description
  • UUID

You can test the action under the Test tab by selecting the destination and clicking Test.

If destination is not visible, Go to Control Tower view of Build and select Destinations and add the destination you created before.

Do these steps to create three actions to fetch root, item and stop information. Idea here is, first fetch root and then PRD item. From item node, get the FU and go to FU stop to get acceptable and planned dates. Provide all this information to Joule for analysis.

While creating action for item,

  • add a filter to restrict only PRD items.
  • Reduce the Output to have only freightUnitUUID field.

While creating action for stop,

  • Reduce output to pick only location, stoprole, stopcategory,acceptable start and end time and planned time.

STEP 6: Define Joule Skill

Navigate to Build Lobby and click create and select Joule Agent and skill. Once the project is created, click create and select Joule Skill. Provide a clear name and description of the skill.

Click on conversation starter and provide the prompt. Example ‘get execution blocked freight order with stop details and analyze the reason for block’

 

You don’t need any other input from user as we already did filter in our action to pick execution blocked freight orders.

Add the action by clicking the ‘+’ button and select our action to fetch freight order root.

 

Navigate to skill parameter (select anywhere in the editor and click >> button to view skill parameter). Select the output for http 200 code as shown below.

 

Finally bind the skill output to the trigger end of action.

 

Likewise create other skills to fetch item and stop nodes.

For item skill,

  • Skill input must be TransportationOrderUUID
  • Map skill input to action input as shown below

 

  • Finally map skill output to trigger end.

For stop skill,

  • Skill input must be FreightUnitUUID
  • Map skill input to action inputs shown below

  •  

STEP 7 – Create Joule Agent

In the project, create ‘Joule Agent’ and navigate to agent definition screen.

Define ‘Expertise’ which provides the persona of the agent and ‘Instructions’ as system prompt on how to analyze reason for blocked freight order. Write that in plain, simple English. An example as shown below.

 

Provide some few-shot learnings to the agent as part of instructions. Example below

##Example 1 (case with date 'TranspOrdStopPlanTranspDteTme' is before date 'TranspOrdStopAccptblStrtDteTme')

Given the following Freight unit stop details:

- Transportation stop acceptable start date: 10-January-2026

- Transportation stop acceptable end date: 12-January-2026

- Transportation stop planned date: 8-January-2026

// Business Rule: date 'TranspOrdStopPlanTranspDteTme' must be after date 'TranspOrdStopAccptblStrtDteTme'

// Analysis: 8-January-2026 is NOT after 10-January-2026

// Expected blocked freight order Analysis result: Since planned date is not after acceptable start dates, freight order is blocked

Select your desired LLM provider, base and advanced model. Example OpenAI, GPT-4o Mini and GPT-4o. Save the agent definition.

Navigate to the Tools tab and add the three skills to the Agent you created before,

 

At the end, your project will have one Joule Agent and three Joule Skills.

 

STEP 8: Testing!

Click on the Test icon at the top of the project. Select the actual destinations within BTP to be used at runtime.

The conversation starter will appear and click that.

 

The agent will:

  • Select the required skills
  • Execute them in the appropriate sequence
  • Map parameters between skills
  • Evaluate the data
  • Return a business-friendly analysis using the selected LLM

 

 

Summary:

This example demonstrates how easy it is to build custom Joule agents and skills.
The same approach can be applied to other S/4HANA solutions and a wide range of use cases.

This blog should help anyone new to Joule get started and build a simple proof of concept.

entry.title: Creating a ‘Hello World’ Joule Agent
entry.content:
Building on Michael Ameling's excellent Agent Builder in Joule Studio announcement and The Joule Studio Learning Series, this post will guide you through building your first Joule Agent.

I'll walk you through the steps to build a "Hello, World" agent. Along the way, you'll get familiar with the basic workflow in SAP Build, explore the UI, avoid at least one common pitfall, and have your agent up and running in just a few minutes. By building the simplest possible agent, you'll gain the confidence that building agents is easy, and creating more sophisticated ones will feel like a natural next step. Let's get started.

Setup and Prerequisites
The setup of SAP Build Apps, the activation of Joule, and the SAP Agent Builder are described in these two blog posts:
  • How to Get Started with Joule Studio
  • Activate Joule Studio in 5 Simple Steps

I'll assume that's done, and we'll start our journey in the lobby of SAP Build Apps.

Creating a Project
Click on the "Create" button, and select "Joule Skill":
 
 
Enter a name and a description:
 

Creating the Joule Agent

You'll be forwarded to the overview of your project where you can create the Joule Agent:

 

Again, enter a name and a description. A proposal for the identifier will be generated automatically:

 
On the details page of your Hello World Agent, you could fill in the fields manually, but let's use Joule to create a proposal. In the top left, click on the Joule icon to open the Joule sidebar. Enter a prompt like this:

"Can you please update our existing Hello World agent by filling in the expertise, instructions and additional context? The agent should respond to every prompt with "Hello, World!"."

 
 
As a result, Joule updates the agent, and we're almost done. We just need to add a placeholder tool, for example the calculator, because Joule Studio does not allow an agent to be saved without a tool assignment:

 
Now you can save the agent, and we can move on to testing the functionality we've just implemented.

 

Testing the Joule Agent

When you click on the "Test" button (just above the "Save" button), you'll be asked which environment you'd like to test in. Select the environment associated with your email address.

If your email address doesn't appear in the dropdown, you need to activate your private environment first. To do so, click on the SAP Build icon in the top left corner, click on "Control Tower" in the left-hand menu, and then click on the "Environments" tile:

On the Environments screen, click the button to activate your private environment:

Afterwards, you can resume testing and your private environment should appear in the dropdown as described above.

Now we're ready to test the agent, for example with a prompt like "Let's test the agent".

 
 
As we can see, the agent correctly responds with "Hello, World!" 😅

To end the test session, just click on the "Stop Testing" button.

Deploying the Joule Agent

To get our agent out of the testing environment, we need to deploy it to a real environment.

Let's create a Hello World environment. Navigate to the Control Tower, select the Environments tile, and click on "Create". Enter a name and description for the environment. The proposal for the identifier will be generated automatically.

 

Your user will be automatically added to this new environment. If you see a blank screen when you want to view the environment details, just try refreshing the page in the browser. It may take a little while to generate.

Once the environment is active, we can deploy our agent. Click on the "Release" button in the agent overview.

 

In the subsequent pop-up, enter a release note and click on "Release".

 

Once released, switch to version 1.0.0 at the top of the screen by clicking on the dropdown next to the title.

 
 

In the released version, there is a "Deploy" button instead of the "Test" and "Release" buttons. Click on the "Deploy" button, select the Hello World environment, and click on "Deploy".

 
 
After a few moments, the status of agent version 1.0.0 will change to "Deployed and Active".

Testing the Deployment

As a final step in this tutorial, let's test our deployed agent in the Hello World environment.

Open the Hello World environment via the Control Tower and view the environment details by clicking on it in the list. There, you will see the deployment of the Hello World agent we just made.

To test it, open the Joule tab for this environment. Depending on your screen resolution, this may be hidden in the "More" drop-down. On this tab, click the "Launch" button.

 

Joule will open in a new tab and we can prompt it to test the agent, for example like this: "Run the Hello World agent."

To confirm that Joule actually called the agent, you can investigate the log by clicking on the icon in the top right of the title bar.

 
 

Conclusion

Congratulations, you just implemented your first Joule agent! As intended, the overall result is "just" a Hello World agent, but this is an important first step in your journey to becoming a Joule agent builder. You familiarized yourself with the UI and performed the full workflow from start to finish, including creating a project, creating an agent, testing, and deploying it. Along the way, we also used Joule itself to fill in the agent's configuration details.

From here, there are many more topics worth exploring, like Joule skills, MCP integration, or agent-to-agent communication. However, for me, it's always important to build a Hello World example first without getting lost in the details. With more complex starter scenarios, it's easy to get stuck on technical details and lose sight of the big picture. Now that you've completed your "Hello World", you can iteratively add more features and build more sophisticated agents. What's the first use case you're going to tackle?

entry.title: SAP Build Apps Deprecation and The Path Forward
entry.content:
Hello,
My name is Patrick Schad, and I’m a Product Manager for SAP Build. In this post, I’d like to share important updates about the evolution of SAP Build Apps, what these changes mean for you, and how we’ll support your transition to our unified platform.

 

What's happening?

As part of the continued evolution and simplification of the SAP Build portfolio, SAP Build Apps is being deprecated as a standalone product. Moving forward, customers can leverage SAP Build unified offering, that combines application development, process automation, and business site creation into a single platform that supports low-code, code-first, and generative AI capabilities. 

 

What does this mean to you?

We recognize that change is never easy, and decisions like this are made with careful consideration. We are here to help outline what it means for you and your organization and are committed to supporting you every step of the way throughout this transition.

As of 23rd of March 2026, SAP Build Apps will be retired. Please note that there is no immediate impact on existing customers. Whether you have BTPEA/PAYG/CPEA or subscription-based licensing, you will continue to have full access to SAP Build Apps for the duration of your current contract. We will honor all existing commitments, including SLAs and maintenance, and your service will remain fully supported and operational through the end of your agreement.

 

Why are we making this change and what is the path forward?

Going forward, customers can leverage SAP Build offering, which unifies application development, process automation, and business site creation into a single platform that supports low-code, code-first, and generative AI capabilities.

It also allows us to focus our engineering and product investments where they can drive the greatest value and impact for your organization.

If you're currently using SAP Build Apps, now is the time to explore how SAP Build can empower your teams with its advanced capabilities. This transition ensures you have access to the latest features, and alignment with SAP’s innovation roadmap.

SAP Build Apps Frontend Projects

As you plan your next steps, we recommend leveraging the pro-code capabilities within SAP Build to recreate and further evolve your current and future applications. Our teams are here to support you throughout this process and help identify the best approach for your specific use cases.

In your SAP Build Apps backend project, open each entity in the data browser and use the Export option to download your data as a .csv file. Repeat this step for each entity.

In your new CAP project within SAP Build, import the downloaded .csv files. (Prerequisite: ensure that a table with the relevant fields has already been created in your CAP backend.)

entry.title: Reimagining the Customer Journey with AI-Powered SAP Sales and Service Excellence
entry.content:
📌  Introduction

How modern enterprises are weaving together intelligent automation, real-time knowledge, and seamless cross-platform workflows to deliver frictionless customer experiences.

In today’s digital-first world, customers expect fast, personalized, and seamless service experiences. Traditional disconnected systems often lead to delays, inefficiencies, and poor customer satisfaction.

To address this, organizations are adopting intelligent, integrated solutions that connect sales, service, and backend operations. By leveraging platforms like SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2, SAP S/4HANA Cloud, and SAP Field Service Management, along with AI capabilities, businesses can deliver a unified and proactive customer journey.

This blog demonstrates an end-to-end process that integrates AI, automation, and enterprise applications to optimize customer experience from initiation to closure.

💼  Business Use Case

Consider a scenario where a customer encounters an issue with a product and begins by attempting to resolve it through a self-service portal. If the issue remains unresolved, a case is created and handled by a service agent, supported by intelligent recommendations and knowledge systems. As the interaction progresses, the situation may evolve into a potential sales opportunity, enabling the organization to propose a suitable solution or upgrade. A quote is then generated and shared with the customer, who can review and sign it digitally, ensuring a seamless and efficient agreement process.

Once confirmed, backend systems take over to process the order and initiate service fulfillment. This includes creating the necessary orders and coordinating with field service operations, where a technician is assigned for on-site support. The technician completes the required service, resolves the issue, and updates the system, leading to the closure of the case.

This end-to-end use case demonstrates how organizations can transform traditional support interactions into revenue-generating opportunities, while automating backend processes, improving response and resolution times, and delivering a truly seamless, cross-functional customer experience.

🏗️   Architecture

The solution integrates multiple systems across the customer journey:


Frontend & Experience Layer
SAP Build Apps
• Self-service capabilities for customers
Customer Engagement Layer
SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2
• Case Management • Opportunity Management • Quote Management • AI-assisted troubleshooting
AI & Knowledge Layer
eGain Knowledge Management
• Intelligent Q&A • Knowledge Base search • Similar case suggestions
Digital Signature Integration
DocuSign
• Seamless agreement processing • Digital contract signing
Backend ERP Layer
SAP S/4HANA Cloud
• Solution Order • Sales Order • Delivery • Billing
Field Service Layer
SAP Field Service Management
• Service Call • Technician Assignment • Field execution

⚙️  Key Capabilities and Business Benefits

  • 🤖AI-Driven Self-Service : Automated issue identification and resolution suggestions
  • 📚Intelligent Knowledge Management : Context-aware recommendations using knowledge base
  • 🔄End-to-End Process Integration : Seamless flow from case → opportunity → quote → order → service
  • ✍️Digital Contract Management : Faster approvals using DocuSign
  • 🔧Smart Field Service Execution : Automated technician assignment and scheduling

📋  Prerequisites

Before implementing this end-to-end solution, it’s important to have the right landscape, integrations, and development setup in place.

🔧  Core Systems

Ensure access to the following key solutions:

  • SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 for case, opportunity, and quote management
  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud for backend order processing and billing
  • SAP Field Service Management for service execution and technician handling

🔌  Integration Layer

  • Middleware or API-based integration using SAP BTP (recommended)
  • Connectivity with DocuSign for digital agreements
  • Integration with eGain Knowledge Management for knowledge and AI-driven recommendations

🧠 AI Enablement

  • Configured and structured knowledge base
  • AI services enabled for intelligent Q&A, recommendations, and case insights

👨‍💻Development & Extension Setup

  • Use CAP (Cloud Application Programming Model) to build custom microservices, autoflow logic, and backend extensions on SAP BTP
  • Develop UI applications using SAP Fiori for a consistent and enterprise-ready user experience
  • Expose and consume APIs for seamless communication between frontend, AI services, and backend systems

The step journey, unpacked

The flow is built around four macro-phases — Initiate, Assess & Troubleshoot, Resolve, and Closure — each supported by a distinct set of SAP and partner tools.

Step 1: Self-service

The customer lands on a self-service portal before ever reaching a human. Intelligent Q&A, powered by eGain Knowledge Management, deflects simple queries instantly.

Step 2 : Case creation

When self-service can't resolve the issue, a case is created in SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2. AI surfaces similar past cases and searches the knowledge base automatically.

Step 3: Opportunity

A service case becomes a commercial opportunity. Agents can pivot from problem-solving mode to solution-selling without switching systems.

Step 4 : Quote + DocuSign

A quote is generated and sent for e-signature via DocuSign — all within the same workflow. No email attachments, no context switching.

 

Step 5 : Solution order

In our Scenario we are using Sales order and Service Order

Once signed, the solution order in S/4HANA  is created and downstream fulfilment is triggered automatically.

 

Step 6 : Sales order fulfilment

SAP S/4HANA Cloud handles the sales order, delivery, and billing — a direct integration that eliminates re-keying of data.

Step 7 : Service order

In parallel, a service order is raised for any physical work that needs to happen on-site.

Step 8 : Service order replication

The service order is replicated into SAP Field Service Management, keeping every system consistent without manual effort.

Step 9 : Service call

A service call is initiated in SAP FSM, formally opening the field engagement.

 

Step 10 : Technician assignment

The right technician is assigned based on availability, skills, and location — the field team arrives prepared and resolve this issue

🏁Conclusion

This end-to-end flow demonstrates how organizations can transform customer journeys using AI and integrated enterprise platforms. By connecting sales, service, and backend operations, businesses can deliver faster, smarter, and more efficient customer experiences.

entry.title: From SAP Build Apps to SAP Build: Rethinking Low-Code Development in the SAP Ecosystem
entry.content:
SAP Build Apps has its roots in SAP’s acquisition of AppGyver, a powerful no-code platform that enabled rapid application development without traditional coding.

What SAP Build Apps Enabled

  • Drag-and-drop UI creation – This is much appreciated by the business
  • Visual logic flows – Good to visualize compared to syntax of the code
  • Mobile-first app design – It matters because 60% of the traffic is from mobile devices
  • Citizen developer empowerment – You have an idea – Voila – then start building!

It played a key role in:

  • Democratizing application development as the business users can build if it is a simple use case
  • Accelerating prototyping – Accessibility accelerated prototyping and check
  • Enabling business-led innovation – democratizing the application development & prototype acceleration enabled the innovation that can be business led.

SAP Build Apps followed a flat architecture, where UI and logic were tightly coupled, making it ideal for simple applications but limiting for enterprise-scale solutions. In the current scenario of ecosystem, while simplicity to build the apps helps but it hinders scale or prevents from building complex enterprise-scale solutions.

And here comes the ‘sunset of SAP Build Apps’ as a standalone strategic tool and it is not a step backward — it is a strategic evolution.

Key Drivers Behind the Transition

  1. From UI-Centric to Process-Centric Development

Organizations today require:

  • Workflow-driven applications rather than UI centric. The UI should be really in alignment with the workflow.
  • Automation-first solutions

SAP Build Apps was primarily: UI-focused, not process-driven

  1. Need for Workflow Orchestration

Modern enterprise apps demand:

  • Approval workflows – If processes are waiting for approvals, then the delay/wait time is inducing lag in creation of value to the business.
  • Task routing – We do not need manual intervention to route the tasks the orchestration should happen automatic for non-critical routing of tasks.
  • Process monitoring – Command center set up has become important for the businesses so that process monitoring can be done to understand the non-value adding sub-processes.

These capabilities require a dedicated process layer, which was not native to SAP Build Apps.

  1. Integration as a First-Class Requirement

Applications must seamlessly connect with:

  • SAP S/4HANA
  • APIs
  • External ecosystems

SAP Build Apps had limited enterprise integration capabilities.

  1. Unified Development Experience

SAP’s strategic direction is to unify:

  • Low-code
  • Pro-code
  • Automation
  • AI

into a single platform.

Enter SAP Build: The Unified Platform

SAP Build represents SAP’s next-generation development environment.

 What SAP Build Brings Together in summary -

Capability Description

App Development

Build responsive UI applications

Process Automation

Workflow, approvals, business rules

Workspaces

Business sites and launchpads

Pro-Code Extensions

CAP, APIs, advanced logic

AI Integration

Joule-powered assistance

SAP Build introduces a layered architecture, separating UI, process, and backend — enabling scalability and maintainability.

Use Case: Let us take one example and understand better.

Purchase Requisition is the most common Application

Let’s examine a simple yet powerful scenario:

Business Flow:

  1. Employee creates a purchase request
  2. Manager reviews the request
  3. Approval or rejection decision
  4. Status tracking

SAP Build Apps vs SAP Build: A Practical Comparison

Deep Dive: Application Behavior

Process-driven, auditable, scalable, enterprise-ready

Conclusion

SAP Build Apps was instrumental in enabling rapid innovation and empowering citizen developers.

However, as enterprise requirements evolved, SAP Build emerged as the strategic platform, offering:

entry.title: From SAP Cloud ALM Alerts to AI-Powered Recommendations
entry.content:
In my previous blog, I covered how SAP Cloud ALM alerts can be enriched and routed using SAP Build Process Automation. The main idea was to go beyond the standard SAP Cloud ALM email notification and create a more flexible process where we can define recipients, enrich the message, and send a customized notification to the right support team.
In this blog, I would like to take the same concept one step further.

The flow would look like the following:

SAP Cloud ALM Alert
→ Operation Flow / Operations Automation
→ SAP Build Process Automation workflow triggered
→ BPA Calls SAP AI Core
→ SAP AI Core Orchestration
→ Extract AI Result & saves in a variable
→ Send enriched email notification

The idea is that an SAP Cloud ALM operation flow sends the alert payload to SAP Build Process Automation. From that payload, we pass selected values into a script task, which builds a prompt for SAP AI Core. SAP AI Core then returns recommended corrective actions, which we insert into the email body.

Step 1: Create the SAP AI Core action

In SAP Build -> Actions tab, create  a custom action for SAP AI Core.

The action uses: 
Method: POST
Endpoint: /v2/completion

The destination points to the SAP AI Core orchestration deployment URL, for example:
https://api.ai.<server>.com/v2/inference/deployments/<deployment-id>

The destination uses OAuth2ClientCredentials and contains the required headers, for example:
AI-Resource-Group = default
Content-Type = application/json

In the action body, most values are static, such as the model and configuration. The important dynamic input is the prompt content.

Then test the action, if successful, generate the output structure and publish the action.

Step 2: Create the SAP Build Process Automation process

In my configuration, the process contains the following steps:

Receive CALM Payload
→ Script task to Build AI Prompt
→ Custom Action 
→ Script task to Extract AI Result
→ Send Mail
→ End

Step 3: Build the AI prompt

Before calling SAP AI Core, I added a script task called "Build AI Prompt". The script reads values from the SAP Cloud ALM payload and transforms into a prompt

Example logic:

var eventName = $.context.startEvent.eventName;
var rating = $.context.startEvent.rating;
var serviceName = $.context.startEvent.serviceName;
var eventSubType = $.context.startEvent.eventSubType;
var eventBody = $.context.startEvent.body;

var aiPromptText =
"You are an SAP Cloud ALM Operations expert. " +
"Provide only recommended corrective actions for the support team. " +
"Do not repeat the full alert summary. " +
"Event name: " + eventName + " " +
"Rating: " + rating + " " +
"Service: " + serviceName + " " +
"Event subtype: " + eventSubType + " " +
"Technical details: " + eventBody;

$.context.custom.aiprompt = aiPromptText;

Step 4: Map the prompt to the SAP AI Core action

In the action step, I mapped:

content = Custom Variables 

This means the generated prompt is passed to SAP AI Core at runtime

Step 5: Extract the AI result:

The SAP AI Core response contains the generated recommendation under the final_result object. Since the response can include a list of choices, I used a script task to extract the first generated response and store it in a custom variable.

Simplified example:

var choices = $.context.action_post_postV2Completion_1.result.final_result.choices;

var aiResultText = "No AI-generated recommendation was returned.";

if (choices && choices.length > 0 && choices[0].message && choices[0].message.content) {
aiResultText = choices[0].message.content;
}

$.context.custom.aifeedback = aiResultText;

I also split the AI response into separate custom variables for each recommended action. This helped improve the email formatting

Step 6: Build the custom email

Use the previously created variables and also splitting the AI answer into separate variables is useful because rich-text email editors may not always preserve line breaks inside one long variable.

entry.title: Learning SAP Build Process Automation: My Beginner Guide & Hands-on Practice (Part 1/2)
entry.content:
If you are just starting out with SAP Build Process Automation or preparing for the Developing with SAP Build Process Automation learning journey, you might feel like there is a lot of concepts to absorb at once.

When I first went through the study material, I realized that reading the theoretical documentation alone only gave me a general idea. The real "understanding!" moment happened when I started working on the exercises myself.

If you have little to no background in UI design or workflow development, don't worry—SAP Build is designed so you don't need extensive coding skills In this two-part blog series, I want to share my hands-on experience and walk you through building a Purchase Requisition Approval Process step-by-step.

What is SAP Build Process Automation?

Before we dive into the exercise, let's briefly look at what SAP Build Process Automation actually does.

At its core, it enables organizations to digitize and automate business workflows visually—without writing complex code. Using an intuitive drag-and-drop process designer, you can quickly build end-to-end workflows complete with:

  • Trigger Forms: To collect user input.
  • Approval Tasks: To route items to managers or approvers.
  • Decision Rules: To automatically approve or reroute requests based on conditions (like amount or priority).

A real-world example: Consider a purchase requisition scenario where an employee submits a request through a form. The system evaluates the purchase amount or priority, and the workflow automatically routes the request for approval, auto-approval, or rejection based on predefined rules. By automating these steps, organizations reduce manual effort, eliminate email back-and-forth, and accelerate decision-making.

Let's Practice Together!

Now that you have the general context, let's put theory into practice! I encourage you to follow along in your own SAP Build environment so you can experience how intuitive the tools really are.

Tutorial Overview & Objective

We will build, deploy, and run a Purchase Requisition Process in three incremental stages across this series:

Part 1 (This Post): Basic Approval Process (Setting up the environment, trigger form, process metadata, and manager approval).

Part 2 (Next Post): Enhanced Routing & Auto-Approval Rules (Adding approval/rejection forms and conditional logic).

In this first tutorial, we will build Part 1 of our Purchase Requisition Approval Process.

Our Roadmap for Stage 1:

  1. Setting up the environment in Control Tower.
  2. Creating the Employee Trigger Form to gather initial request data.
  3. Configuring Process Metadata (Subject lines, dynamic variables, and recipients).
  4. Building the Manager Approval Form and mapping inputs.
  5. Releasing, deploying, and testing our live workflow!

Prerequisites: Setting Up Your Environment

Before creating your project, make sure you set up your destination environment in the Control Tower:

  1. Navigate to SAP Build Dashboard → Control Tower → Environments.
  2. Click Create Environment, give it a unique Name and Identifier, and save. (You will deploy to this environment after you release your work.)

Task 1: Building the Basic Approval Process
Step 1: Create the Project & Process

  1. From the SAP Build Dashboard, click Create → Process Automation → Build Process Automation Project.
  2. Name your project (e.g., Purchase Requisition Process) and click Create.
  3. Inside your project overview, click Create → Process. Provide a name and identifier, then click Create.

Step 2: Build the Trigger Form

  1. In the Process Builder, click Add a Trigger → Submit a Form → Create a New Form.
  2. Name your form (e.g., PR Request Form) and click Open Editor.
  3. Drag and drop the following fields into the layout:

Step 3: Configure Process Panel & General Settings

When you select the process canvas, review the Process Panel on the right side:

  • Business Key (General Tab): Map this to dynamic process variables like Employee Name or Priority. This uniquely identifies your process instances inside the Monitoring tab when tracking running requests.
  • Subject: Enter Request from [Employee Name] (using the variable picker to insert the input variable). This acts as the task title in the recipient's inbox so approvers immediately see who submitted the request.
  • Recipients: For testing and exam practice, select Started By.
    Tip: Why Started By? In a production environment, you would assign this to a specific manager group or dynamic role. In a testing scenario, setting Started By routes the task back to you so you can act as the approver and test your own workflow end-to-end!

     

     

     

Step 4: Create the Manager Approval Form

  1. Click the (+) icon directly under the Trigger step in your process flow.
  2. Select Approval →  Blank Approval Form. Name it Manager Approval Form and click Create.
  3. Open the approval form editor and add the exact same fields as the Trigger form, but set all fields to Read-Only.

Step 5: Map Inputs & Form Metadata

Step 6: Release, Deploy, and Test!

  3. Choose the Environment you created in the Control Tower step.
  4. Once deployed, open your Trigger step, copy the Form Web Link, and paste it into a new tab.
  5. Fill out the form, hit submit, and head over to My Inbox (or your SAP Build Task Center) to view your live approval task!
